hints: Square both sides to find $x$ in terms of $y$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = \sqrt{x} - 1$ and isolate the radical term:
$$\sqrt{x} = y + 1$$

Square both sides to make $x$ the subject and swap variables:
$$x = (y + 1)^2 \implies f^{-1}(x) = (x + 1)^2$$

hints: Analyze $g(x) = \frac{1}{x^2+2}$: what is its maximum when $x = 0$?
Explain whether $g$ is one-to-one or many-to-one to determine if $g^{-1}$ exists.
walkthrough:
Determine the maximum and limiting values of $g(x) = \frac{1}{x^2+2}$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$\text{Since } x^2 \ge 0, \text{ the minimum denominator is } 0 + 2 = 2 \implies \max(g(x)) = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{As } x \to \pm\infty, \frac{1}{x^2+2} \to 0 \text{ from above} \implies g(x) > 0$$
$$\text{Range of } g: 0 < g(x) \le \frac{1}{2}$$

Explain the existence of the inverse function $g^{-1}$:
$$g^{-1} \text{ does not exist because } g \text{ is not one-to-one (it is many-to-one, e.g. } g(1) = g(-1) = \frac{1}{3}\text{)}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Ranges of Functions: States the correct range $0 < g(x) \le \frac{1}{2}$ (B1). Explains that $g^{-1}$ does not exist because $g$ is many-to-one / not one-to-one / fails horizontal line test (B1).

hints: Equate denominators to get $(\sqrt{x}-1)^2 = 2$, solve for $\sqrt{x}$, and square to get $x = a + b\sqrt{c}$.
walkthrough:
Equate denominators and solve for $\sqrt{x}$:
$$(\sqrt{x}-1)^2 + 2 = 4 \implies (\sqrt{x}-1)^2 = 2$$
$$\text{Since } x > 1 \implies \sqrt{x}-1 > 0, \text{ take positive root: } \sqrt{x}-1 = \sqrt{2} \implies \sqrt{x} = 1 + \sqrt{2}$$

Square both sides to find $x$ in the exact surd form $a + b\sqrt{c}$:
$$x = (1 + \sqrt{2})^2 = 1 + 2\sqrt{2} + 2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{2}$$

ai_rubric.Composite Functions: Evaluates $f(25/16) = \frac{1}{4}$ (B1). Sets up $\frac{1}{(\sqrt{x}-1)^2+2} = \frac{1}{4}$ (M1). Solves for $\sqrt{x} = 1+\sqrt{2}$ (M1). Obtains exact result $x = 3+2\sqrt{2}$ (A1).
